title: How to Choose a WordPress Theme
description: A practical framework for choosing a WordPress theme around content, editing workflow, performance, and long-term maintenance.
metaDescription: A practical KreativWP guide to choosing a WordPress theme for a durable, maintainable site.
intro: A strong theme choice starts with how a site needs to work after launch. This guide is a practical decision framework, not a ranked list or a claim that one theme fits every WordPress site.

sections.title: Start with the editing workflow
sections.body: Choose around the way your team creates pages, posts, patterns, and reusable site elements—not around a feature list alone. A theme that looks right in a demo can still be a poor fit for the people who have to update it.

sections.title: Separate essentials from extras
sections.body: Write down the site capabilities you genuinely need: blog layouts, navigation, commerce, portfolio work, multilingual support, or a pattern library. Treat everything else as a trade-off, not an automatic advantage.

sections.title: Check the complete stack
sections.body: A theme is only one layer. Evaluate it with the editor, plugins, host, content volume, image strategy, analytics, and devices that will make up the actual site. Avoid judging performance from a theme demo alone.

sections.title: Look at maintenance before launch
sections.body: Review update practices, documentation, support boundaries, export options, and how much custom code the project will need. A lighter initial setup is not useful if ordinary edits become fragile later.

sections.title: Make a small proof site
sections.body: Before migrating a production site, build a representative page and one real content workflow in a staging environment. Record what was installed, what changed, and what still needs custom work.
